title: Arbitrary free V2 NFT mint via fake ERC20 (primeToken check removed)
description: V2 removed the V1 invariant that validates `token == dispatcher.primeToken()`. V2 source even has comment at line 166: "V2: No primeToken() validation — transfers whatever token the user specifies." An attacker deploys a malicious ERC20 where `balanceOf` returns 0 and `transferFrom` returns true without moving funds. Then `balanceBefore=0`, `transferFrom` "succeeds", `balanceAfter=0`, `actualReceived=0`. The subsequent `dispatch(address(this), 0, extraData)` on GatherV2 transfers 0 WBTC (valid zero-transfer), on BurnerV2 calls `IBurnable(_token).burn(0)` (no-op), and `_mint(recipient, resolvedTokenId, 1, "")` issues the NFT for free. The attacker can repeat indefinitely.
impact: Anyone can mint arbitrary V2 claim NFTs for free, dilating all legitimately minted NFTs and effectively breaking the protocol's claim-entitlement invariant. Directly matches the user's concern "no arbitrary V2 NFT minting through exploits."
recommendation: Restore V1's check: `require(ITokenDispatcherV2(config.dispatcher).primeToken() == token, "mismatch")`. Alternatively, bind each dispatcher config to a fixed expected token and validate the caller-supplied `token` against it.
